data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Miscellaneous systemic drugs_

**Class:** Aldosterone antagonist (potassium-sparing diuretic) with anti-androgenic activity

## Mechanism of action
- Blocks androgen receptors in sebaceous glands and hair follicles; reduces ovarian/adrenal androgen synthesis (inhibits 17α-hydroxylase); increases SHBG

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Acne in adult women (especially jawline/hormonal, PCOS) — 'off-label first-line hormonal therapy'
- Hirsutism, female pattern hair loss, hidradenitis suppurativa in women

## Dose & formulations
- Acne: 50–100 mg/day (25–200 mg range); hirsutism/FPHL: 100–200 mg/day; results in 3 months
- Often combined with combined oral contraceptives (prevents menstrual irregularity, provides contraception)

## Adverse effects
- Menstrual irregularity, breast tenderness, diuresis, dizziness, postural hypotension
- Hyperkalaemia — rare in young healthy women (routine K⁺ checks not needed per recent guidance); check in renal disease, older patients, ACE inhibitor/ARB users
- Gynaecomastia in men (not used for men's acne)
- Animal tumour data (high doses) — not seen in humans

## Contraindications
- Pregnancy (feminisation of male fetus), hyperkalaemia, renal failure, Addison disease; men (gynaecomastia)

## Drug interactions
- ACE inhibitors, ARBs, potassium supplements, trimethoprim, NSAIDs (hyperkalaemia); digoxin levels rise

## Monitoring
- Potassium only if risk factors; BP

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated in pregnancy — use with contraception.

## Viva points
- Anti-androgen for female acne and hirsutism
- Routine potassium monitoring not needed in healthy young women
- Pregnancy — feminisation risk

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.34 (Antiandrogens); Khopkar (Antiandrogens). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
